**Pathology Report** **Patient:** James Miller **MRN:** 001234567 **Sex/Age:** Male / 61 y **Specimen ID:** RLU‑CORE‑001 **Specimen Type:** CT‑guided core needle biopsy – right lower lobe lung mass **Clinical Information:** 61‑year‑old man with a 4.5 cm right lower lobe pulmonary mass (CT) concerning for primary lung carcinoma. No prior systemic therapy. --- ### Gross Description - **Number of cores:** 5 - **Length of cores:** 1.2 cm, 1.0 cm, 0.9 cm, 0.8 cm, 0.7 cm (total tissue 4.6 cm) - **Appearance:** Tan‑white, firm, focally hemorrhagic. - **Fixation:** 10 % neutral buffered formalin, processed in routine fashion. --- ### Microscopic Description Sections reveal infiltrating malignant epithelial cells forming irregular glandular structures and occasional lepidic‑type growth. The tumor cells exhibit moderate nuclear atypia, prominent nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasmic mucin. Mitotic activity is brisk (≈8/10 HPF). No necrosis is identified in the limited sample. The background lung parenchyma shows focal emphysematous change without evidence of granulomatous inflammation. --- ### Immunohistochemistry (IHC) – Performed on biopsy material | Marker | Result | Interpretation | |--------|--------|----------------| | TTF‑1 (clone 8G7G3/1) | Positive (nuclear) | Supports pulmonary adenocarcinoma | | Napsin A | Positive (cytoplasmic) | Supports adenocarcinoma lineage | | CK7 | Positive (cytoplasmic) | Consistent with lung primary | | p40 | Negative | Excludes squamous differentiation | | CK5/6 | Negative | Excludes squamous differentiation | | ALK (D5F3) | Negative | No ALK protein expression | | PD‑L1 (22C3) – Tumor Proportion Score | 10 % | Low‑level expression | --- ### Molecular Testing (Results available on same specimen) -

| CK7 | Positive (cytoplasmic) | Consistent with lung primary | | p40 | Negative | Excludes squamous differentiation | | CK5/6 | Negative | Excludes squamous differentiation | | ALK (D5F3) | Negative | No ALK protein expression | | PD‑L1 (22C3) – Tumor Proportion Score | 10 % | Low‑level expression | --- ### Molecular Testing (Results available on same specimen) - **EGFR mutation analysis (PCR):** No sensitizing mutations detected. - **KRAS, TP53, STK11, CDKN2A:** Testing not performed on this specimen; results pending from separate NGS assay. --- ### Diagnosis 1. **Primary lung adenocarcinoma, right lower lobe** – invasive, moderately differentiated (based on glandular architecture and cytologic features). 2. **Immunophenotype:** TTF‑1+, Napsin A+, CK7+, p40‑, CK5/6‑, ALK‑, PD‑L1 TPS 10 %. **Comment:** The immunoprofile is characteristic of a primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma. EGFR mutation testing is negative. Molecular profiling (e.g., KRAS, TP53, STK11, CDKN2A) is recommended to further define actionable alterations. of stage IIA (T2aN1M0) large‑cell non‑small cell lung carcinoma, right lower lobe, resected 2 years prior. - Completed adjuvant Platinol/vinorelbine chemotherapy. - Recent imaging (contrast‑enhanced CT chest) demonstrated a 3.2 cm right hilar mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy, concerning for recurrent disease. **Gross Description:** Four cylindrical core fragments, each measuring 0.5–0.9 cm in length and 0.2–0.3 cm in diameter, are received in formalin. The cores are tan‑white, firm, and show focal areas of necrosis. All tissue is submitted in its entirety for histologic evaluation. **Microscopic Description:** Sections reveal a malignant neoplasm composed of sheets and nests of large polygonal cells. The tumor cells display: - Abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm - Vesicular nuclei with coarse chromatin and prominent nucleoli - Marked nuclear pleomorphism - Frequent mitoses (≥15 per 10 high‑power fields) - Focal geographic necrosis No glandular differentiation, mucin production, or keratin pearl formation is identified. The background lung parenchyma shows chronic inflammatory changes but no residual in‑situ component. **Immunohistochemistry (Ancillary Studies):** | Marker | Result | Interpretation | |--------|--------|----------------| | Cytokeratin 7 (CK7) | Positive (diffuse, strong) | Supports pulmonary epithelial origin | | p40 (ΔNp63) | Positive (diffuse, strong) | Consistent with squamous lineage, commonly expressed in large‑cell carcinoma with squamous differentiation | | Thyroid transcription factor‑1 (TTF‑1) | Negative | Excludes typical adenocarcinoma phenotype | | Napsin A | Negative | Supports non‑adenocarcinoma histology | | EGFR (immunostain) | Negative (no membranous staining) | Correlates with prior molecular testing showing EGFR wild‑type | | Ki‑67 (MIB‑1) | High proliferative index (~70 %) | Reflects aggressive behavior

lower lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection (adjuvant cisplatin + vinorelbine completed) - Disease recurrence at age 68 with right hilar mass, mediastinal nodes, left adrenal nodule, and three brain metastases (treated with stereotactic radiosurgery) **Specimen:** - **Type:** CT‑guided core needle biopsy - **Site:** Right hilar mass (right lung) - **Diagnosis (histology):** Large‑cell carcinoma, CK7⁺, p40⁺, EGFR IHC negative **Test Performed:** - **Assay:** Hybrid‑capture DNA‑based NGS panel (covers > 500 cancer‑relevant genes, including SNVs, indels, copy‑number alterations, and selected fusions) - **Platform:** Illumina NovaSeq 6000 - **Library Prep:** DNA extracted from formalin‑fixed, paraffin‑embedded (FFPE) tissue; average unique coverage 550×; ≥ 99 % of targeted bases ≥ 100× - **Quality Metrics:** % On‑Target Reads = 92 %; Mean Insert Size = 180 bp; Molecular Barcode Consensus Accuracy > 99.9 % --- ### Genomic Findings | Gene | Alteration | Nucleotide Change | Protein Change | Variant Allele Frequency* | Classification | Clinical Significance | |------|------------|-------------------|----------------|---------------------------|----------------|-----------------------| | **KRAS** | Missense (SNV) | c.34G>T | p.G12C | 28 % | Pathogenic | FDA‑approved KRAS G12C inhibitors (sotorasib, adagrasib) in metastatic NSCLC; eligibility for KRAS‑targeted clinical trials | | **TP53** | Missense (SNV) | c.818G>A | p.R273H | 45 % | Pathogenic | Associated with poorer prognosis and aggressive disease biology; no direct targeted therapy | | **STK11** | Splice‑site alteration | c.291+1G>A | Predicted loss‑of‑function | 30 % (estimated) | Pathogenic | Correlates with reduced response to PD‑1/PD‑L1 checkpoint blockade; potential enrollment in trials exploring STK11‑directed strategies | | **CDKN2A** | Homozygous deletion (copy‑number loss) | – | –

**PATHOLOGY REPORT** **Patient:** Eleanor Martinez Sex: Female Age: 65 y **Specimen ID:** RL‑CORE‑001 **Specimen Type:** CT‑guided core needle biopsy – right lower lobe lung mass **Clinical History:** 65‑year‑old woman with a 5 cm right lower lobe pulmonary mass on imaging, concerning for primary lung carcinoma. --- ### Gross Description - Four core biopsy fragments received, total combined length 2.5 cm. - Cores are tan‑white, firm, and measure 0.4–0.8 cm in length. - Specimen is inked, fixed in 10 % neutral buffered formalin, and submitted in standard cassettes. ### Microscopic Description - Sections reveal infiltrating malignant epithelial cells forming irregular glandular structures with both acinar and lepidic patterns. - Tumor cells display enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and moderate cytoplasmic vacuolization. - Mitotic activity is increased (≈6/10 HPF). - No necrosis identified in the sampled cores. - Background lung parenchyma shows focal emphysematous change, without evidence of granulomatous inflammation. ### Immunohistochemistry (IHC) | Marker | Result | Interpretation | |--------|--------|----------------| | TTF‑1 (nuclear) | Positive (strong, diffuse) | Supports pulmonary origin | | CK7 (cytoplasmic) | Positive (diffuse) | Consistent with adenocarcinoma | | Napsin A | Positive (moderate) | Supports lung adenocarcinoma | | p40 | Negative | Excludes squamous differentiation | | ALK (IHC) | Negative | No ALK protein expression | | ROS1 (IHC) | Negative | No ROS1 protein expression | | PD‑L1 (22C3, TPS) | 20 % (tumor proportion score) | Low‑intermediate expression | ### Molecular Testing (NGS – 500‑gene panel) - **KRAS:** G12C mutation, variant allele frequency (VAF) 34 % –

**Liver:** New 1.6 cm lesion in segment VII (previously 1.5 cm), SUV 7.5 on prior PET, now slightly larger → **progression** of hepatic metastasis. - **Other pulmonary nodules:** Sub‑centimeter, stable. - **No new osseous lesions.** **Impression:** - Progressive hepatic metastasis (increase from 1.5 cm to 1.6 cm) despite docetaxel therapy. - Pulmonary primary and mediastinal disease remain stable. --- ### Assessment 1. **Stage IV KRAS‑G12C adenocarcinoma of the lung** – hepatic progression on third‑line docetaxel; pulmonary disease stable. 2. **Treatment‑related toxicities:** - Grade 2 peripheral neuropathy (persistent, attributable to prior paclitaxel). - History of grade 3 neutropenia (resolved; current ANC adequate). 3. **Performance status:** ECOG 1, functional but limited by fatigue and dyspnea. 4. **Laboratory profile:** Mild anemia, stable renal function, slight rise in CEA. --- ### Plan 1. **Systemic Therapy** - **Hold docetaxel** pending discussion of next‑line options. - Review eligibility for clinical trials targeting KRAS‑G12C (e.g., sotorasib, adagrasib) and for immunotherapy‑based combinations given PD‑L1 TPS 20 %. - If trial enrollment not feasible, consider a non‑platinum doublet (e.g., vinorelbine‑ or gemcitabine‑based) with dose adjustments for renal function; discuss risks/benefits with patient. 2. **Supportive Care** - Continue **anti‑emetic prophylaxis** (ondansetron 8 mg PO q8h PRN). - **G‑CSF** (filgrastim) prophylaxis for next chemotherapy cycle if a myelosuppressive regimen is chosen, given prior neutropenia. - **Neuropathy management:** Gabapentin 300 mg TID, monitor for efficacy and side effects. - **Fatigue:** Encourage moderate activity as tolerated, consider low‑dose dexamethasone 4 mg PO BID for short term if fatigue worsens. 3. **Laboratory & Imaging Follow‑up** - CBC, CMP, and CEA
